newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine says could sign Australian gold mine deal.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says could sign Australian gold mine deal.

text.p: Ukraine could join forces with Australia's RGC by the end of the year to mine the Myzhiyevsky gold, silver, lead and zinc deposit, Deputy Industry Minister Serhiy Hryshchenko said on Monday.
"We have a protocol to negotiate with RGC," Hryshchenko told a news conference. "There could be a joint venture formed by the end of the year."
He gave no details of the potential deal except to say that RGC's investment could be as much as $30 million.
The industry ministry is overseeing work on the deposit, in western Ukraine, as part of a programme to develop a gold industry by 2001.
Hryshchenko said the deposit -- which is expected to yield two to three grams of gold a tonne -- was richer in lead, zinc, cadmium and silver.

Hryshchenko said 22 foreign companies from Australia, Canada, the United States and Great Britain had expressed interest in exploring Ukrainian gold deposits in the eight months since the former Soviet republic announced its gold programme.
"Ukraine is not the Klondike, and it's not South Africa, but the gold industry can be profitable and it can be respectable," he said. "With foreign investment the industry will be profitable."
Ukraine's gold deposits were barely developed in Soviet times.
The government last month decided it would take a 51 percent stake in all companies set up to identify and explore gold deposits and that it would license gold mining activities.

State gold mining concern Ukrzoloto is exploring three deposits in the Trans-Carpathian region, near the border with Hungary. But Hryshchenko said richer deposits had been located in the eastern Dnipropetrovsk area.
Initial gold production, planned for 1997, is expected to total 900 kg (31,800 ounces) and Ukraine hopes to produce 12-15 tonnes annually in three to four years.
